questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word segment in the given sentence. If the sentence is grammatically correct, select ‘No correction’.

The book, which has all the details on parenting, **missing. **
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The highlighted phrase "**missing**" is incomplete and does not fit the structure of the sentence properly.
 
• The correct verb form to indicate the current state of the book's unavailability is "**is missing**."
 
• The use of "is missing" ensures the sentence is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning clearly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The book, which has all the details on parenting, **is missing**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **No correction** – This option would be correct if the original sentence was grammatically accurate, but it is not since "missing" alone is incomplete.
 
• **Had been missing** – This implies a past action that is no longer true, which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Had missing** – This is grammatically incorrect as it does not follow standard English syntax.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

**The software was developed in** a team of experts and tested by users before its release.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition "**by**" is the most appropriate choice to indicate the agents or people responsible for the action (in this case, the team of experts).
 
• Using "**across**" or "**at**" in this context would be incorrect, as they do not align with the intended meaning of collaboration or creation.
 
• The preposition "**on**" also does not fit the context, as it generally refers to working on a specific task or subject, not indicating the creators.
 
• Thus, "**by**" correctly conveys that the software was developed by a team of experts.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The software was developed **by** a team of experts and tested by users before its release."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "*developed across*" – Incorrect, as "across" implies a physical space or area, which is not relevant here.
 
• **Option 2:** "*developed at*" – Incorrect, as "at" refers to a specific location, which is not the focus here.
 
• **Option 4:** "*developed on*" – Incorrect, as "on" is unsuitable for describing the creators of the software.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Don't assume that everyone but you is happy. The __grass is always redder on one side__.

options.text: sky is red in the evening
grass is always greener on the other side
plant is always greener on all sides
fruit is yellow on the other side

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "grass is always greener on the other side".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"grass is always greener on the other side"** is an idiom that means people often believe that others have it better or easier, even though this may not be true. (दूसरों की स्थिति या चीजें हमेशा बेहतर लगती हैं, भले ही ऐसा न हो।)

 
 
• **Example:** He quit his stable job thinking the grass is greener on the other side, but soon realized the challenges of freelancing.
 
 

 
• **Explanation:** In the given sentence, "The grass is always redder on one side" does not make sense. The correct idiom is "grass is always greener on the other side," which fits the context and conveys the intended meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Sky is red in the evening** (सूर्यास्त के समय आकाश लाल होता है): This is a literal statement and not an idiom. It refers to the natural phenomenon of the sky appearing red due to the scattering of sunlight.

 
 
• **Example:** The sky is red in the evening during sunset.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Plant is always greener on all sides** (पौधा हमेशा सभी तरफ हरा होता है): This is not a recognized idiom in English. It is an incorrect variation of the actual idiom.
 
• **Option 4: Fruit is yellow on the other side** (फल दूसरी तरफ पीला होता है): This is also not an idiom and has no relevance to the context of the sentence.
